lines.text: ܕܐܬܬܚܕܘ : ܘܠܐܢܫܝܢ ܗܠܝܢ ܕܡܢ ܩܠܝܪܘܣ ܥܡܗܘܕܝܐ
lines.en: which were seized: and to those men of the clergy with the Jews

lines.text: ܕܪܒ ܟ̈ܗܢܐ ܫܩ̣ܠܢ : ܥܒܕܐ ܕܢܘܪܐ ܠܩܘܒܠܢ ܚ̈ܘܝܠܢ :
lines.en: of the chief priests we took: the work of fire against us they showed:

lines.text: ܘܩܕܡܘܗܝ ܕܗܝܟܠܐ ܕܒܬܘܠܬܐ ܩܕܝܫܬܐ ܝܠܕܬ ܐܠܗܐ
lines.en: and before the temple of the holy virgin, mother of God

lines.text: ܡܪܝܡ : ܟܕ ܟܠܢܫ ܒܗܘܢ ܒܟ̈ܬܒܐ ܕܚܪ̈ܫܘܬܐ ܚ̇ܙܐ ܗܘܐ
lines.en: Mary: while everyone in them in the books of sorcery was seeing

lines.text: ܕܝܩܕܝܢ : ܘܕܫܐܕ̈ܐ ܕܝ̇ܩܕܝܢ . ܘܫ̈ܡܥܝܢ ܗܘܘ ܠܗܘܕܡ ܒܝܕ
lines.en: that they were burning: and of the demons that were burning. And they were hearing to him by

lines.text: ܗܠܝܢ ܕܩ̇ܪܐ ܗܘܐ : ܗ̇ܘ ܕܠܗܢܘܢ ܠܢܘܪܐ ܡܫܕܪ ܗܘܐ :
lines.en: those things which he was reading: he who to them to the fire was sending:

lines.text: ܫܘܒܗܪܗܘܢ ܕܗܠܝܢ ܕܟ̈ܬܝܒܢ ܗ̈ܘܝ : ܘܫܘܥܠܝܐ ܕܠܐ ܐܠܗ
lines.en: their boasting of those things which were written: and the questioning of no god

lines.text: ܘܒܪܒܪܝܐ ܘܡܘܠܟܢܐ ܒܝ̣ܫܐ ܘܣܢܝܐ ܒܚ̈ܢܢܫܐ ܕܝ̇ܕܥܐ :
lines.en: and barbarian and the evil and hateful promise in men who know:

lines.text: ܘܪܡܘܬܐ ܕܐܟܠܩܪܨܐ : ܗ̇ܝ ܕܫܘ̈ܕܝܐ ܕܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ
lines.en: and the pride of the devil: that of promises which like these

lines.text: ܡ̈ܪܝܪܐ ܘܣܢܝ̈ܐ ܐܠܦ . ܐܝܬܝܗܘܢ ܗܘܘ ܓܝܪ ܗܠܝܢ
lines.en: bitter and hateful he taught. For they were these

lines.text: ܫܘ̈ܕܝܐ ܕܐܝܟ ܗܠܝܢ ܀ ܐܝܟܢܐ ܙܕܩ ܕܢ̈ܬܕܠܚܢ ܡܕܝ̈ܢܬܐ
lines.en: promises which like these: How it is right that cities should be disturbed
and that peoples should be moved: how fathers against

lines.text: ܒܢ̈ܝܐ : ܘܠܩܘܒܠ ܒ̈ܢܝ ܒܢ̈ܝܐ ܗ̇ܘܘ ܐܝܟܢܐ ܢܫܬܪܘܢ .
lines.en: sons: and against sons of sons they should be how they should be loosed.

lines.text: ܘܕܒܐܝܠܝܢ ܦܘ̈ܪܣܐ ܢܫܬܪܘܢ ܙܘ̈ܘܓܐ ܢܡܘܣܝ̈ܐ ܘܫܘܬܦܘ̈ܬܐ
lines.en: And by what means lawful marriages and partnerships be dissolved

lines.text: ܕܐܒܝܚܘܬܐ : ܘܕܐܝܟܢܐ ܢܫܕ ܩܛܝܪܐܝܬ ܢܟܦܐ ܐܢܬܬܐ
lines.en: of fornication: and how a chaste woman be cast violently

lines.text: ܕܢܟܦܘܬܐ ܪܚܡܐ ܕܬܚܐ : ܠܘܬ ܪܚܡܬܐ ܠܐ ܢܡܘܣܝܬܐ .
lines.en: who loves chastity that she should live: to unlawful love.

lines.text: ܐܘ ܐܝܟܢܐ ܓܘܪܐ ܘܩܛܠܐ ܚܨܝܦܐܝܬ ܐܘ ܓܢܒܘܬܐ
lines.en: Or how adultery and murder impudently or theft

lines.text: ܬܬܛܫܐ . ܘܕܒܐܝܠܝܢ ܙܢ̈ܝܐ ܐܢܫ ܢ̣ܐܠܨ ܠܕܝ̈ܢܐ ܕܕܝܢܐ :
lines.en: should be hidden. And by what kinds a man should compel the judges of judgment:
that the decree of victory they should decree for him.

sections.text:
“ Libros magicos, iam prehensos, tunc comburendos curavimus.
Idcirco, defensore (ἔκδικος) urbis, magistratibus (οἱ τοῦ δημοσίου)
clericisque iussu episcopi nobiscum abductis, ignem ante templum
Virginis sanctae genitricisque Dei Mariae accendimus, unoquoque
magorum libros operaque daemonum flagrantia aspiciente atque
audiente antea, per ea quae legebantur ab eo qui (scripta) ista in
ignem coniiciebat, rerum exaratarum iactantiam, atque daemonum
arrogantiam impiam et barbaram, promissionemque malam et
generis humani odio imbutam, atque diaboli superbiam, qui promissa
facinoraque tam horribilia docuit. Erant enim promissa ista talia :
“ Quomodo urbes turbandae, et populi commovendi, et patres
armandi sunt contra filios nepotesque „ ; et “ quibus artibus solven
tur coniugia legitima concubinatusque „ ; et “ quo pacto aliquis vi
mulierem caste vivere cupientem ad amorem illegitimum seducet „ ;
vel “ quomodo adulterium et homicidium audacter impetrabuntur
aut furtum celabitur „ ; et “ quanam ratione aliquis iudices coget ut
causam sibi adiudicent „.
sections.en: “ We then took care that the magical books, already seized, should be burned. Therefore, with the defender (ἔκδικος) of the city, the magistrates (οἱ τοῦ δημοσίου) and the clerics led away with us by the order of the bishop, we lit a fire before the temple of the holy Virgin and mother of God Mary, with each one of the magicians watching the books and works of the demons burning and hearing beforehand, through those things which were read by him who was throwing those (writings) into the fire, the boasting of the things written down, and the impious and barbarous arrogance of the demons, and the evil promise imbued with hatred of the human race, and the pride of the devil, who taught such horrible promises and deeds. For those promises were such : “ How cities are to be disturbed, and peoples stirred up, and fathers are to be armed against sons and grandsons ” ; and “ by what arts lawful marriages and concubinages are dissolved ” ; and “ by what means someone by force will seduce a woman desiring to live chastely to unlawful love ” ; or “ how adultery and murder will be boldly obtained or theft concealed ” ; and “ by what method someone will compel judges to adjudge a case to himself ”.

summary.headline: Burning of Magical Books
summary.text: An account of seized magical books burned before the temple of the Virgin Mary, describing their demonic boasts and malicious promises: stirring cities and peoples to rebellion, dissolving marriages, seducing chaste women, concealing adultery, murder, and theft, and coercing judges.
